trigger.cause: Isolate the reslice from threading: same 8 CPUs and STAN_NUM_THREADS=1 as the 53,001 s baseline, so only the slicing differs. (The reslice's rationale, that reduce_sum copies shared parameter arguments, was never validated.)

evidence.slurm_array_vs_raw_ids: Task 25581035_0 has raw job id 25581037 and task 25581035_1 has raw id 25581035. The first array element carries the LATER raw id.

tasks.note: D~29. Last logged progress 5,200/16000 (raw job log, read earlier in the session).
D~99. Last logged progress 2,900/16000 (raw job log). About 157 iterations/h by cumulative average against about 62/h for the single-thread original; both include warmup, so indicative only.

deviations.CANCEL_REASONS_WERE_BASED_ON_MISLABELLED: The D~29 task (raw 25581037) was cancelled at 6h33m because I took it for D~99 with fewer than 100 iterations. The D~99 task (raw 25581035) was then cancelled at 18h27m because I read the cancelled D~29 job's frozen log as a 12-hour stall of the live D~99 job. Neither cancellation was justified by the jobs' actual state. Retracted 2026-10-13.
deviations.reslice_effect: UNRESOLVED, leaning faster at D~99 (about 2.5x by cumulative iterations per hour); inconclusive at D~29 because the original's early-phase timeline is unrecoverable (W&B keeps only the console tail). The reslice was reverted on the models branch feat/stan-three-level on the strength of the mistaken result, and that revert's message quotes the retracted numbers.
deviations.source: Slurm facts (state, elapsed, node, CPUs, submit time) come from sacct as read on 2026-10-13; cohort, host and W&B run id come from each run's W&B config. The two agree on node and duration for every job. sacct truncates the cancelling uid, so who issued each scancel is not recoverable from it; the causes below are the reasons stated at the time and are marked where they were later found wrong.
